actual_author_read_scope: All scientific text L0–622, tables and captions reread; reference list retained. No raw PDF or figure rasters.

claims.paraphrase: PKO1 chromosomal donor DNA was assayed mainly in P. aeruginosa PAO1.93 catA clones. Those hosts are not native pathway taxa.

Deletion mapping supports tbuE/F/G/K/I/H/J order and corresponding ring-cleavage, hydrolytic, oxidative, aldolase, decarboxylase, tautomerase and hydratase activities. The terminal acylating dehydrogenase was not mapped.
tbuS in trans restored repression without inducer and induction with phenol. TbuR concerned the upstream phenol hydroxylase. Direct effector binding and promoter occupancy were model interpretations.
Phenol and m-cresol induced extract activities; tested catechols and other cresols did not. Noninduction is not enzyme inhibition or inability to metabolize after induction.
Catechol and both methylcatechols were ring-cleavage substrates. Heterologous methylcatechol growth used phenol inducer and was reported without displayed data.
Promoter-region deletion abolished downstream activities despite trans regulator complementation. Ring-cleavage-only clones accumulated yellow semialdehyde.

limits: Do not upgrade donor-gene expression to whole-route proof in P. aeruginosa or proof of a seventh acylating step in PKO1.
Exact modern substrate stereochemistry was not established.
